title: Meaningful commits and branches
learningObjectives: Complete meaningful commits and branches using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: A meaningful commit groups one coherent change and uses a message that explains its purpose. Branches isolate work so features and fixes can be reviewed before integration. Small focused commits are easier to inspect and revert.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear history supports debugging, collaboration, and controlled releases. Avoid mixing unrelated changes in one commit.
understand.analogy: A commit is a labelled checkpoint; a branch is a separate work lane for a focused change.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The commands create a focused branch and record one coherent change. Review staged changes before committing.

examples.code:
# Example:
git switch -c feature/bookmarks
git add public/js/bookmarks.js
git commit -m "Add lesson bookmark state"
examples.explanation: The commands create a focused branch and record one coherent change. Review staged changes before committing.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Create a feature branch and make two small commits with clear messages. Review the diff before merging.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.

Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
